title: Lawgivers and the unschooled crowd
source_text: Μετὰ ταῦτα πάλιν λοιδορεῖται τῷ πρεσβεύοντι χριστιανισμὸν καὶ ἀποφαίνεται μὲν περὶ αὐτοῦ ὡς καταγέλαστα διεξιόντος, οὐκ ἀποδείκνυσι δὲ οὐδὲ ἐναργῶς παρίστησιν ἅ φησιν εἶναι καταγέλαστα. καὶ λοιδορούμενος οὐδένα φρόνιμόν φησι πείθεσθαι τῷ λόγῳ, περισπώμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ πλήθους τῶν προσερχομένων αὐτῷ. ὅμοιον δὲ ποιεῖ καὶ ἐν τούτῳ (τῷ) φάσκοντι διὰ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν κατὰ τοὺς νόμους ἀγομένων ἰδιωτῶν ὅτι φρόνιμος οὐδεὶς, φέρ᾿ εἰπεῖν, Σόλωνι ἢ Λυκούργῳ πείθεται ἢ Ζαλεύκῳ ἤ τινι τῶν λοιπῶν, καὶ μάλιστα ἐὰν φρόνιμον λαμβάνῃ τὸν κατ᾿ ἀρετὴν ποιόν. ὡς γὰρ ἐπὶ τούτων κατὰ τὸ φανὲν αὐτοῖς χρήσιμον οἱ νομοθέται πεποιήκασι τὸ τοιαύτῃ ἀγωγῇ αὐτοὺς περιβαλεῖν καὶ νόμοις, οὕτως νομοθετῶν ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ὁ θεὸς τοῖς πανταχοῦ ἀνθρώποις καὶ τοὺς μὴ φρονίμους ἄγει, ὡς οἷόν τε ἐστὶν ἄγεσθαι τοὺς τοιούτους ἐπὶ τὸ βέλτιον. ὅπερ. ὡς καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀνωτέρω εἰρήκαμεν, ἐπιστάμενος ὁ ἐν Μωϋσεῖ θεὸς λέγει τό· „αὐτοὶ παρεζήλωσάν με ἐπ᾿ οὐ θεῷ. παρώργισάν με ἐν τοῖς εἰδώλοις αὐτῶν· κἀγὼ παραζηλώσω αὐτοὺς ἐπ᾿ οὐκ ἔθνει, ἐπ᾿ ἔθνει ἀσυνέτῳ παροργιῶ αὐτούς,“ εἰδὼς δὲ καὶ ὁ Παῦλος εἶπε· „τὰ μωρὰ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελέξατο ὁ θεὸς , ἵνα καταισχύνῃ τοὺς σοφοὺς,“ „σοφοὺς“ κοινότερον λέγων πάντας τοὺς δοκοῦντας προβεβηκέναι μὲν ἐν μαθήμασιν ἀποπεπτωκότας δὲ εἰς τὴν ἄθεον πολυθεότητα· ἐπεὶ „φάσκοντες εἶναι σοφοὶ ἐμωράνθησαν, καὶ ἤλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ ἀφθάρτου θεοῦ ἐν ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος φθαρτοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πετεινῶν καὶ τετραπόδων καὶ ἑρπετῶν.“
pass_a_gloss: After these things again he reviles (λοιδορέομαι) the one championing (πρεσβεύω) Christianity, and declares (ἀποφαίνομαι) about him as recounting (διεξέρχομαι) laughable things (καταγέλαστα), but does not demonstrate (ἀποδείκνυμι) nor clearly (ἐναργῶς) present (παρίστημι) what he says are laughable. And reviling he says no sensible man (φρόνιμος) is persuaded by (πείθομαι) the doctrine (λόγος), being drawn aside (περισπάομαι) by the multitude (πλῆθος) of those coming to it. He does the like in this to one saying, because of the multitude of laymen (ἰδιῶται) led (ἄγω) according to the laws (νόμοι), that no sensible man, say, obeys Solon or Lycurgus or Zaleucus or any of the rest, and especially if he takes 'sensible' as the one qualified (ποιός) by virtue. For as in their case, according to what appeared useful (χρήσιμον) to them, the lawgivers (νομοθέται) have made it [their aim] to surround (περιβάλλω) them with such training (ἀγωγή) and laws, so legislating (νομοθετέω) in Jesus God leads, for men everywhere, also those not sensible, as such are able to be led toward the better (τὸ βέλτιον). Which, as we said also above, knowing, God in Moses says: 'they moved me to jealousy (παραζηλόω) with no god; they provoked me (παροργίζω) with their idols (εἴδωλα); and I will move them to jealousy with no nation (ἔθνος); with a senseless (ἀσύνετος) nation I will provoke them' [Deut 32:21]. And knowing [it] Paul also said: 'the foolish things (τὰ μωρά) of the world (κόσμος) God chose (ἐκλέγομαι), that he might shame (καταισχύνω) the wise' [1 Cor 1:27], calling 'wise' more commonly all seeming to have advanced (προβαίνω) in learnings (μαθήματα) but having fallen (ἀποπίπτω) into godless (ἄθεος) polytheism (πολυθεότης); since 'claiming to be wise they became foolish (μωραίνομαι), and exchanged (ἀλλάσσω) the glory of the incorruptible (ἄφθαρτος) God in the likeness (ὁμοίωμα) of an image (εἰκών) of corruptible (φθαρτός) man and birds and quadrupeds and reptiles' [Rom 1:22-23].
pass_b_english: After this he again abuses the man who champions Christianity, and pronounces that he recounts laughable things, but he does not prove, or even clearly set out, the things he calls laughable. In his abuse he says that no sensible man is persuaded by the teaching, being misled himself by the great number of those who come to it. In this too he acts like a man who would say, because of the great number of unschooled people who are guided by the laws, that no sensible man obeys, let us say, Solon or Lycurgus or Zaleucus or any of the others, and especially if he takes “sensible” to mean the man whose character is shaped by virtue. For just as with such people the lawgivers, according to what seemed useful to them, put them under such a discipline and such laws, so God, giving laws in Jesus to men everywhere, guides even those who are not sensible, so far as such people can be guided toward the better.

The God who speaks in Moses knew this, as we have also said above, and says: “They moved me to jealousy with what is no god; they provoked me to anger with their idols; and I will move them to jealousy with what is no nation; with a senseless nation I will provoke them to anger” (Deuteronomy 32:21). Knowing it, Paul too said: “God chose the foolish things of the world to put the wise to shame” (1 Corinthians 1:27). By “the wise” he means, in a broad sense, all who seem to have advanced in learning but have fallen away into godless polytheism, since “claiming to be wise, they became fools, and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man and birds and four-footed beasts and creeping things” (Romans 1:22–23).

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 73 (Koetschau 3.73). Celsus's charges are reported indirectly (φησι + infinitive; ὡς + participle) and are not set in quotation marks. περισπώμενος is nominative and goes with Celsus: he is misled by the number of converts; rendered 'being misled himself'. (τῷ) is an editorial supplement. Solon (Athens), Lycurgus (Sparta) and Zaleucus (Locri) are the Greek lawgivers. 'As we have also said above' points back to an earlier use of Deuteronomy 32:21 in this work (e.g. Book 2.78). Deuteronomy 32:21 LXX quoted exactly ('senseless nation' renders ἔθνει ἀσυνέτῳ, which answers Origen's point about guiding 'those who are not sensible', μὴ φρόνιμοι). 1 Corinthians 1:27 and Romans 1:22-23 quoted exactly (ἐν ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος, 'for the likeness of an image').
Checked against the Perseus TEI 3.73: complete

'Knowing this, as we have also said above, God speaks in Moses' to 'The God who speaks in Moses knew this, as we have also said above, and says' (ὁ ἐν Μωϋσεῖ θεός is the subject; ἐπιστάμενος a participle)
'a foolish nation' to 'a senseless nation' (ἔθνει ἀσυνέτῳ; keeps the link to οἱ μὴ φρόνιμοι); translator note updated
Confirmed the 'said above' reference: Deuteronomy 32:21 is also quoted in Book 2.78
Deuteronomy 32:21, 1 Corinthians 1:27 and Romans 1:22-23 verified clause by clause
